title: Multi-granular economic decomposition + timelag reconciler for per-route/model/customer breakdowns
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a deterministic, auditable service that produces per-route / per-model / per-customer cost and latency breakdowns with configurable time windows (1m, 5m, 1h, daily) and a reconciliation layer to account for event arrival timelags and late-joining telemetry. This ticket covers the backend computation and reconciliation logic: event ingestion normalization, attribution heuristics (token-level vs request-level), multi-pass apportionment for shared resources (prefix cache hits, batching credits), and the TTL/retention strategy for final and partial slices.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Service outputs a stable monthly and hourly breakdown for a sample tenant that matches golden invoices within 0.5% for token-count-based costs and within 3% for latency-weighted adjustments.
2) Late-arriving events (up to 72h) are reconciled into existing slices without creating duplicate records or double-charging.
3) Exposes incremental streaming endpoints for the Console and a bulk backfill job for historical fixes.
4) API supports query by route, model, customer, and arbitrary tag dimensions.
5) End-to-end tests + performance benchmark show pipeline can sustain 10k req/s at 95th p50 latency target for the aggregator (<200ms for aggregation path).
tech_notes:
Data sources: token-level traces from runtime, model-cost profiles from model catalog (cost per token/seq), route metadata from console routing rules, KV cache hit events, batching credits from serving runtime.
Key design choices considered: deterministic vs probabilistic apportionment; we choose deterministic two-pass allocation: first-assign firm costs (model compute, dedicated capacity shares), then apportion shared benefits (cache hits, batching) proportional to estimated token-exposure.
Storage: denormalized hourly shards in BigTable/Spanner-like store (row key: yyyyMMdd:hour:route:model:customer). Use compacted OLAP view in Redshift/ClickHouse for analytics and console queries.
Reconciliation: maintain 'watermark' per tenant, run idempotent update transactions keyed by event-hash. Late events apply delta records and emit tombstone-style corrections to downstream consumers.
Observability: expose per-shard counters, reconciliation lag histogram, ghost-correction rate metric, end-to-end checksum that can compare "as-of" views to canonical invoice sample.
Privacy/Security: tenant isolation in storage, KMS encryption at rest for PII. Security review required due to billing impact.
migration_plan:
Phase 1: Shadow compute - run service in parallel with existing rollup for 2 weeks on 5 pilot tenants (no consumer surface changes).
Phase 2: Read-only surfaced to Console as "preview" with disclaimers for 1 month.
Phase 3: Swap downstream consumers to new table and enable delta corrections. Provide a backfill job to recompute last 90 days using Spark job.
Rollback: maintain feature flag to route Console to previous rollup; corrective backfill script to revert if mismatch > threshold.
rollout_plan: Canary on 5 high-volume tenants -> 25 tenants -> org-wide opt-in -> full default. Monitor cost-delta and reconciliation corrections; hold if >2% unexplained deltas observed for 24h.
monitoring_plan: Dashboards: per-tenant reconciliation-lag, corrections/sec, daily-cost-delta, aggregation-latency-95p. Alerts: recon-lag > 1h for >5% tenants, correction-rate spike > 0.1% of events, aggregation job failures. Post-deploy QA run comparing sample tenant to billing ledger daily for 7 days.
